facts.text: All of this has been going on for two weeks.
I have a history of COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease).
Four months ago I had a transplant of both lungs, and it went without complications.
I take prednisone 20 mg every day.
I take mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice a day.
I take tacrolimus 5 mg twice a day.
I haven't had any infections recently.
I haven't had any vaccinations recently.
I haven't started any new medicines.

findings.result: Upper extremities: normal. Lower extremities: 3/5, symmetric.

findings.name: spinal MRI
findings.result: Mild degenerative cervical changes without spinal cord compression.

findings.name: electromyography and nerve conduction studies
findings.result: Increased latency and decreased amplitude of the left ulnar sensory and left sural sensory potentials; decreased conduction velocity and amplitude of the left tibial and ulnar motor potentials. Consistent with an acute demyelinating polyneuropathy with axonal changes.

findings.name: tacrolimus trough levels
findings.result: Average 10.5 ± 4.1 ng/mL over the prior 3 months (target trough 8–12 ng/mL).

gold.reasoning: 1. Spinal cord compression was excluded — “MRI of the spine revealed mild degenerative cervical spine disease without evidence of spine compression.” 2. Infection was considered but ruled out — “Urine, blood, and CSF cultures were negative for bacteria, fungi, and viruses, while a repeat serum CMV DNA by PCR was negative.” 3. Tacrolimus-induced polyneuropathy was considered but deemed unlikely — “Although nerve conduction studies in patients with tacrolimus polyneuropathy may also show evidence of demyelinating changes, the symmetric ascending presentation and the absence of a history of elevated tacrolimus levels favor the diagnosis of GBS over tacrolimus polyneuropathy in our patients.” 4. Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy was considered but is less likely given the acute progression — “Symptoms in CIDP tend to progress slowly over eight weeks or several months.” 5. Guillain–Barré syndrome was supported by neurophysiology and CSF findings — “Electromyogram (EMG) and nerve conduction studies showed increased latency and decreased amplitude of the left ulnar sensory and left sural sensory … consistent with an acute demyelinating polyneuropathy with axonal changes.”
